pieces.title: Foundation scaffold
criteria: npm ci && npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm test all pass on a clean checkout
PLAN.md §2 layout exists with real (not empty-stub) core: loop (realtime+manual clock), events, rng, tuning registry, store with versioning, flags, debugApi implementing every §4 method
A playable greybox run: 3 lanes, forward motion, left/right/jump/roll via keyboard and touch swipe, one obstacle type, coins, crash ends run, restart works
tools/capture.mjs implements §5 including --touch and --perf; tools/contact-sheet.mjs works; at least 3 scenarios exist and produce frames+contact.png+trace.json
public/assets/manifest.json + placeholder fallback: deleting/renaming any src never breaks the game; swapping one texture file changes the render with zero code edits
wrangler.jsonc (Workers static assets + worker/ for /api/*) and .github/workflows/deploy.yml exist; `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` succeeds
Devtools are dynamically imported only when flags.devtools; a production build with VITE_DEVTOOLS unset contains no dev panel code

No Subway Surfers / SYBO names, art, sounds or trademarks in shipped game code, assets, UI text, docs/ or build output (dist/). Only the internal planning files PLAN.md and gauntlet/ may name the benchmark as the comparison target; .reference/ stays git-ignored

pieces.title: Camera & world framing
pieces.dimension: Still frames mid-run on a straight section: camera height, distance behind runner, pitch, FOV, where the runner sits on screen, lane width vs runner size, track/rail proportions, curved-world horizon bend, draw distance, fog/atmosphere depth cues, portrait composition. Art fidelity excluded.
pieces.evidence: 6 still frames each: running centre lane, left lane, right lane, mid-jump apex, rolling, approaching a train.

pieces.title: Lane switching feel
pieces.dimension: Frame strips at 30 fps of single and rapid double lane changes: switch duration in frames, easing curve, body lean, camera follow lag and roll, reversal mid-switch, snap/overshoot, how instantly motion begins.
pieces.evidence: Strips: one switch L, one switch R, fast double switch, reversal mid-switch; ≥2 s each.

pieces.title: Jump arc & fast-fall
pieces.dimension: Frame strips at 30 fps: jump apex height relative to runner height, airtime frames, arc shape (rise vs fall asymmetry), camera vertical follow, lane change while airborne, swipe-down fast fall into roll, landing recovery.
pieces.evidence: Strips: plain jump, jump + lane change, jump then slam-down into roll.

pieces.title: Roll
pieces.dimension: Frame strips at 30 fps: roll duration, pose height, entry/exit timing, roll → jump cancel, lane change while rolling, camera response.
pieces.evidence: Strips: plain roll, roll then jump cancel, roll + lane change.

pieces.title: Input responsiveness & chaining
pieces.dimension: How crisply rapid input sequences execute (e.g. left,left,jump,roll within ~1 s): no dropped or delayed actions, motion begins on the first frame after the gesture, buffered actions fire at the right moment.
criteria: Swipe fires when the finger crosses the distance threshold during the move (not on release); threshold and angle tolerance are tunable
Measured input-to-first-motion ≤ 1 sim frame in --touch capture; keyboard identical
Actions issued during a switch/jump/roll are buffered per tuning window and never lost
Works with touch, mouse-drag and keyboard (arrows + WASD + space/shift); no page scroll or zoom on mobile
pieces.evidence: Touch capture of a scripted rapid sequence; trace + strips.

pieces.title: Forward speed & pacing curve
pieces.dimension: Perceived and measured forward speed at run start, ~30 s, ~60 s, ~120 s, ~180 s (sleepers/ties passed per second relative to runner size), acceleration smoothness, top speed.
pieces.evidence: 1-second strips sampled at 0, 30, 60, 120, 180 s.

pieces.title: Runner motion states
pieces.dimension: Readability and timing of runner poses/animation: run cycle cadence, lean into lane change, jump tuck, roll ball, landing squash, stumble recoil, crash. Judged on motion/timing/silhouette, not model quality.
pieces.evidence: Strips of each state.

pieces.title: Obstacle kit & proportions
pieces.dimension: Set of obstacle types and their proportions vs runner and lanes: low barrier (jump or roll), high barrier (roll only), stationary train, oncoming moving train, ramp onto train roofs, roof running, tunnels/overpasses, readability of which action each demands at a glance.
pieces.evidence: Stills of each obstacle type from gameplay camera at ~2 s and ~0.7 s before contact.

pieces.title: Track generation & difficulty ramp
pieces.dimension: Contact sheets sampled every 2 s over the first 3 minutes: obstacle density, pattern variety, fairness (always a path), use of train roofs, coin guidance lines, difficulty ramp.
pieces.evidence: Two 3-minute runs (autopilot/god-mode), frame every 2 s.

pieces.title: Collisions, stumble & crash
pieces.dimension: Frame strips: side-bump stumble (runner deflects back to lane, chaser closes in), second stumble within window = caught, frontal crash sequence, roof edge / ramp leniency, hit-box fairness.
pieces.evidence: Strips: side bump, double stumble catch, frontal train crash, barrier crash.

pieces.title: Chaser (guard + dog)
pieces.dimension: Run start chase, how long chaser stays on screen before falling back, return on stumble, catch sequence, on-screen size/position.
pieces.evidence: Strips: run start 0-6 s, stumble return, catch.

pieces.title: Coins & pickup feedback
pieces.dimension: Coin line layouts (straight, lane-changing, arcs over barriers, on roofs), spacing, height, spin, pickup feedback (flash/sparkle/HUD tick) and pacing of collection.
pieces.evidence: Strips collecting a coin line, an arc over a barrier, a roof line.

pieces.title: Power-ups
pieces.dimension: Jetpack (lift, sky coin line, descent), super sneakers (higher jumps), coin magnet (pull radius/feel), 2x multiplier; pickup presentation, duration timers, end transitions.
pieces.evidence: Strips of each power-up pickup, active state and ending.

pieces.title: Hoverboard
pieces.dimension: Activation (double-tap), board visual state, duration, crash absorbed with board-break effect and brief invulnerability, HUD indicator.
pieces.evidence: Strips: activate, ride, crash absorbed.

pieces.title: In-run HUD
pieces.dimension: Layout, hierarchy and readability at phone size: score + multiplier, coin counter, pause, power-up timers, hoverboard indicator, mission toast; safe areas; number animation.
pieces.evidence: Stills mid-run with and without active power-ups at 540x960.

pieces.title: Home screen & run start
pieces.dimension: Home screen composition (runner idle on track, tap-to-play, navigation to shop/missions/leaderboard/profile/settings, currency display) and the transition from tap into a running game.
pieces.evidence: Home still + strip of tap → running (0-4 s).

pieces.title: Pause, revive & results flow
pieces.dimension: Pause overlay and resume countdown; crash → revive offer (keys) with countdown; results screen (score, coins, best, mission progress, play again/home); timing and clarity of the flow.
pieces.evidence: Stills + strip of crash → revive → results → home.

pieces.title: Missions & score multiplier
pieces.dimension: Mission sets (3 at a time), in-run completion toast, multiplier increase on set completion, daily challenge (original equivalent), clarity of progress UI.
pieces.evidence: Missions screen still, in-run toast strip, multiplier-up moment.

pieces.title: Shop, currencies & upgrades
pieces.dimension: Currencies (coins, keys), character & board catalog with skins, power-up upgrade levels, purchase/equip UX and feedback, progression pacing.
pieces.evidence: Shop stills (characters, boards, upgrades), purchase flow strip.

pieces.title: Leaderboards & online layer
pieces.dimension: Leaderboard/league UI: ranks, player row highlight, tiers/brackets, weekly reset timer, rewards preview.
criteria: LeaderboardService interface with Mock and Http providers selected by VITE_ONLINE_PROVIDER; unit tests for both (Http tested against the Worker via wrangler/miniflare or a fetch mock)
worker/ implements /api/scores (POST, validated, rate-limited) and /api/leaderboard (GET scopes) on D1 with schema.sql and migrations; returns 503 JSON when DB unbound and client falls back to mock
docs/ONLINE.md explains connecting a real D1 database in < 10 steps
pieces.evidence: Leaderboard stills + test output.

pieces.title: Dev cheats panel
criteria: Toggle via ` key and a 3-finger tap / corner long-press on mobile; usable one-handed at 375x812

God mode, no-clip, give coins/keys, unlock all, reset profile, spawn any power-up, activate hoverboard, set speed, time scale (0.1-3x), jump to distance/difficulty, force specific obstacle pattern, show hitboxes, show lane grid, FPS/frame-time/draw-call/memory overlay
Every cheat also callable through window.__game.cheat(name, ...) and covered by a smoke test
Excluded from production bundle unless VITE_DEVTOOLS=1

pieces.title: In-game editor
criteria: Auto-generated from the tuning registry (grouped, searchable, sliders with min/max/step, reset per field) — adding a tuning entry needs zero editor code

Edits player stats, physics/feel, camera, speed curve, spawn weights/difficulty, power-up durations & upgrade tables, skins/equipped items, catalog prices, missions, currencies and profile progression
Live apply mid-run without restart; presets save/load/export/import JSON; persisted across reloads
Usable on a phone (375x812) and desktop; does not tank frame rate while open

pieces.title: Asset swap pipeline
criteria: Every visual/audio/UI asset used by the game is referenced only through the manifest (grep proves no hard-coded asset paths)
docs/ASSETS.md generated from manifest lists every asset with id, file path, format, dimensions/poly budget, pivot/orientation, animation clip names, and a style brief
npm run assets:check validates presence, formats, sizes, glTF clip names and reports placeholders still in use
A critic acting as the art AI swaps one character glb, one texture, one UI icon, one sfx using only docs and succeeds with zero code edits

pieces.title: Audio
criteria: AudioBus on WebAudio with unlock-on-first-gesture, music + sfx buses, mute/volume settings persisted
Synthesized placeholder SFX for jump, roll, lane switch, coin (pitch rises across consecutive pickups), power-up, hoverboard, stumble, crash, UI clicks; every sound swappable via manifest
No audio work on the hot path allocates; pauses with visibility

pieces.title: Performance & mobile polish
criteria: --perf capture with 4x CPU throttle at 540x960: p50 ≥ 58 fps, p95 frame ≤ 20 ms over a 60 s run; draw calls ≤ 120; no GC sawtooth > 5 MB
Initial JS ≤ 250 KB gzip (excluding devtools chunk); first playable ≤ 2.5 s on Fast 4G emulation
PWA manifest + icons, standalone portrait, safe-area insets, no rubber-band scroll / double-tap zoom, wake lock during run, pause on visibility change, DPR cap tunable
Landscape/desktop layout letterboxes the portrait playfield gracefully with keyboard hints

pieces.title: Cloudflare deploy from GitHub
criteria: wrangler.jsonc: Workers static assets (SPA fallback) + API worker on /api/*, D1 binding optional
.github/workflows/deploy.yml builds, tests and deploys with cloudflare/wrangler-action on push to main and preview deploys on PRs
npx wrangler deploy --dry-run passes; worker unit tests pass
docs/DEPLOY.md: both GitHub Actions and Cloudflare dashboard Git integration paths, required secrets, custom domain, D1 setup

pieces.title: Full-run gestalt (after merge)
pieces.dimension: Whole-loop comparison: home → start → 3-minute run → crash → revive → results → home. Pacing, flow, responsiveness, feedback density, clarity. Art fidelity excluded.
pieces.evidence: Contact sheets every 2 s plus key-moment strips.
